The writers need only be safe (retries don't corrupt), while the processing function applied during replay must be both idempotent (f(f(x))=f(x)) and commutative (f(x\u2218y)=f(y\u2218x)) so that duplicate entries and reordered entries both converge to the same replayed state. The published distinction between idempotent and safe is thus secondary to the real requirement: the replay function must be a semilattice fold.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log imposes a total order (e.g., sequence numbers), commutativity is unnecessary and only idempotency of the processor suffices","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If events are not reorderable (causal dependencies exist), then the semilattice fold is too strong and the requirement reduces to ordered idempotent processing with deduplication","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the processing function is inherently non-commutative (e.g., event sourcing with state transitions), then duplicates cannot be collapsed by commutativity and the log must enforce exactly-once via idempotency keys","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"An append-only log under at-least-once delivery produces a multiset of events, possibly with duplicates and reorderings. Deterministic replay requires that the processing function F applied to any permutation of this multiset (including multiplicities) yields the same state. This is exactly the definition of a semilattice fold: F is associative, commutative, and idempotent. The writers need only be safe (don't corrupt the log), while F\u2014the replay processor\u2014must satisfy all three algebraic properties. The published idempotent/safe distinction describes writer properties; the actual requirement is on the processor.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
